title: Add replay throttler and stable priming probes to mitigate CUDA-graph capture thrashing
author: Priya Nair
description:
Context: recent rollout exposed intermittent capture thrashing where repeated CUDA-graph capture attempts fail or regress tail latency when traffic has high variance in sequence length. Root cause analysis highlighted two contributing factors: (1) aggressive immediate recapture attempts cause kernel selection oscillation and eviction of warmed KV cache, (2) priming/warmup logic relied on fixed-size priming batches that misaligned with real request length distributions, producing noisy kernel choices. Motivation: avoid full rollback recaptures and reduce warmup flaps by introducing coordinated backpressure for replay attempts and a probe-driven priming stage that aligns KV priming window to workload shape distribution. Summary of changes:
- Introduce a ReplayThrottler in the runtime scheduler that serializes capture attempts per-GPU with exponential backoff and priority slots for already-warmed kernels. The throttler provides a low-overhead consensus (token) to capture drivers so they do not concurrently evict each other.
- Add ProbePriming: lightweight probe requests sent to the capture coordinator to estimate the active sequence-length histogram before running a full priming/capture. ProbePriming adapts probe batch sizes and target sequence lengths based on recent seen distributions and CPU-side sampling to avoid over- or under-priming.
- Implement ResumableCapture: allow an interrupted capture/replay sequence to resume from last-known safe checkpoint (kernel mapping + KV-alignment token) instead of reverting and replaying priming from scratch. This reduces wasted kernel captures on transient failures.
- KV-alignment windows: record KV cache footprints during probes and use soft-shape-alignment guards that are tolerant within a configurable window (default +/- 8 tokens) to reduce false-positive shape mismatches that previously forced recapture.
- Metrics and tracing: new metrics (replay_throttler_backoffs, probe_priming_success, resumable_capture_restarts) and trace spans to help correlate capture activity with tail-latency spikes.
- Tests and canary: unit tests for throttler logic and priming heuristics; an integration canary that runs continuous-batch and burst workloads on a dedicated perf pool.
Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4897) [x] Unit tests added [x] Integration canary completed [x] Backwards-compatible defaults (throttler enabled, conservative windows) [x] Rollback plan: disable throttler or set windows=0 when needed
Impact/risk: changes are opt-in per-deployment via runtime flags; default is conservative to avoid sudden behavior changes. The throttler can increase capture latency for extremely rare long-running captures but reduces oscillation and overall failed recaptures; default parameters tuned against historical traces.
Testing:
- Microbenchmarks: synthetic steady-state and burst tests (see notes_on_benchmarks)
- Canary: 48-hour canary on group-perf-us-west with mixed seq-length traffic; no regression in 95/99/99.9 latencies observed; capture failure rate dropped.
Rollout: staged to main, then to dedicated pools over 2 weeks, with toggles to disable probe priming or resumable capture if incompatibilities observed.
Related: follows up on ENG-4520 and complements previous capture-stability work; not a functional replacement for shape-guard tightening.
Docs: added internal runtime flags docs and console observability mapping.
